stage_a.note: Displays high energy and enthusiasm throughout, smiling broadly and gesturing expressively.
Maintains strong engagement with the pitch content, showing clear excitement about the product's success.
Comes across as highly approachable and relatable when sharing her personal story about her baby.

venture.description: A weighted blanket sleep sack for babies designed to help them feel calm and sleep longer.
venture.note: The product uses gentle weight to increase serotonin and melatonin.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara delivers the prepared presentation, explaining the problem of waking babies and introducing her weighted sleep sack solution.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori expresses amazement and asks if they have samples to look at.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara directs the sharks to the different sizes of samples they have in front of them.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Rob waves and says he is going to sleep, leaving the stage.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: The sharks laugh and wish Rob a good night as he leaves.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara explains the poly-pellet beads inside the sleep sack.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori examines the product and notes the little plastic beads.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara confirms the beads are completely safe, non-toxic, and food grade.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks for clarification on whether the product is essentially a sleep sack with beads.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara confirms Robert's description.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks why her product is better than every other sleep sack.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara begins to explain that there are many sleep sacks on the market.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori interrupts to ask if there are any other sleep sacks that also have beads.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara clarifies that there are no others with beads.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan states that he loves heavy blankets and sleeps much better with them.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan asks if there is scientific research behind it or if it is just obvious.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara deflects the question to ask if she can share her personal story of how the invention started.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert jokes by asking if she can be more specific about the exact date she mentioned.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori laughs at Robert's joke.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara tells the story of her and her husband losing their jobs, creating the prototype, and returning to the topic of science.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara mentions a clinical trial published in October 2018 regarding the product's safety.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan commends her for having clinical trial backing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara adds that she partnered with the woman who published the study for early designs.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks where Tara got the money to pay for the initial development.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara explains she used $14,000 from a maternity leave stipend paid by California that was in a separate account.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark laughs and tells her not to say that out loud.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks if her husband knew she was spending the $14,000.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara admits he didn't really know it was there because it was in another account.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori summarizes that Tara used maternity leave money from the company that fired her to start the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara confirms and says she used the money for a patent pending and prototypes.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks where they are selling, how much they are selling, and the price.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara states that year-to-date they are at about $30,000 in sales.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark acknowledges that the sales figure is not bad.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara adds that they raised about $25,000 from a Kickstarter in June.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks to confirm if $25,000 of the $30,000 total came from the Kickstarter.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara confirms and notes her website has only been live for three weeks.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks how much she sells the product for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara states the price is $79.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan asks what the product costs to make.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara gives the exact manufacturing costs for the small and medium sizes.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks to confirm if those figures are the cost.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara confirms yes.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin states it is not a company yet, just a product, and she needs to build a model; he exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara thanks Kevin.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan praises her inspiration but feels others know the space better, so he exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara thanks Rohan.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark admires her entrepreneurial spirit but finds the product too niche for him, so he exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara thanks Mark.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori offers $100k for 25%, explaining she wants to help license the product to a major baby manufacturer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara acknowledges the offer but pauses to be fair to Robert, who hasn't spoken yet.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert says he loves the story but the business is too early stage for him, so he exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara thanks Robert.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori prompts Tara to make a decision on her standing offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara counters Lori's offer, asking for the same deal but at 20% equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara argues that 20% is huge and compares her potential to another company on track for 90 million.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin interrupts to challenge her valuation comparison, telling her she must be out of her mind.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara defends her statement, asking what if they do get on track to do 90 million.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori reiterates that her offer is a great deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara notes she already came in offering a discount.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori offers to meet her halfway, revising her offer to 22.5% equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tara accepts Lori's revised offer.

turns.speaker: PANEL
turns.summary: The panel celebrates the deal, and Lori and Tara hug.

decisions.note: Not a company yet, just a product, needs to build a model to justify valuation.
Incredible inspiration but not the right shark, others know the space better.
Great entrepreneurial spirit but too niche of a product for him to invest in.
Wants to help license the product to a major baby manufacturer.
Loves the story but the business is too early stage for him.
Counters Lori's offer asking for a slightly lower equity stake.
Meets the founder halfway between 20% and 25%.
